title: ERP GPT endpoint knowledge-base document
description: Every file in kb/ (except this one) must validate against this schema. One file per GraphQL endpoint, named exactly after the endpoint: topCustomers.json documents topCustomers. CI enforces that every endpoint in the GraphQL schema has a matching KB file. RULE: no business data anywhere in these files — endpoint documentation only.

endpoint.description: Exact GraphQL field name, camelCase. Must match the schema.

family.description: Which ARGUMENT style this endpoint takes. The Query Plan builder branches on this — getting it wrong produces a query the API rejects. browse: skip/take/where/order, all optional. detail: a single required id. aggregation: required from/to LocalDate range, plus optional limit or interval.

result_shape.description: Which RESULT shape comes back. NOT derivable from family — salesSummary is an aggregation that returns a single object, not a list. Drives both result parsing and UI rendering (object -> labelled bullet list, list/connection -> table). connection: { totalCount, items[] }. object: one object. list: a plain array.

description.description: One or two plain-English sentences: what this endpoint answers. Write for a salesperson, not a developer.

params.description: Every parameter the endpoint accepts. Empty array if none. The set of required parameters is derived from this list — there is deliberately no separate required_args field to drift out of sync.

type.description: GraphQL type as it appears in the SDL, e.g. Int, LocalDate, String, or an enum name. Note dates are LocalDate, not Date.

required.description: Mandatory. The builder trusts this to decide which arguments it must supply.

example_questions.description: THE HIGHEST-LEVERAGE FIELD IN THIS FILE. These are what get embedded — retrieval matches user questions against these, one vector each. Write them the way sales/finance people actually talk, not developer English. Include at least one Roman-Urdu phrasing where natural. Minimum 4, aim for 5-8. NOT sent to the model after retrieval: their job is done once a match is found.

follow_up_questions.description: Natural next questions to offer once this endpoint has answered. The UI renders these as clickable buttons that append to the prompt. Keep them answerable by an endpoint we actually have.

prompt.description: The full question inserted into the composer when clicked

graphql.description: A complete, valid example query using $variables for parameters. The model copies this shape. It MUST execute against the live schema — CI will run it.

returns.description: Plain-English description of what comes back, e.g. 'List of customer names with summed revenue'.

do_not_use_when.description: Disambiguation against sibling endpoints. If two endpoints could be confused (salesByTerritory vs salesByCategory), this field is how the model tells them apart. Name the endpoint to use instead.

notes.description: Anything else the model needs: date format expectations, limit ceilings, timezone behaviour.
